Action Plan:
- 1. Ensure continued hydration and symptom-focused care for acute diarrheal illness: use oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte), maintain fluid intake, monitor for dehydration, and contact us if diarrhea reaches 6–8 stools per day or if signs of dehydration or poor intake develop.
- 2. Implement a soft, easily digestible diet during diarrhoea: avoid dairy, fish, meat, and eggs while symptomatic; progress to crackers/toast/jam and boiled vegetables with mash as symptoms improve; after 48 hours without diarrhoea, reintroduce meat gradually; consider probiotic yogurts to help restore gut flora.
- 3. Medication considerations and monitoring: review Lexapro as a potential contributor to GI symptoms (SSRI-associated diarrhoea) without changing therapy unless symptoms persist or worsen; no antibiotics unless indicated by investigation or clinical course.
- 4. Red flags, investigations, and follow-up plan: obtain a stool sample if diarrhoea persists for ≥7 days or if blood/mucus appears in stool; reassess urgently if dehydration develops, if fever is high, or if symptoms worsen; document and review notes in the patient app; follow up as needed.
- 5. Documentation/consent: Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Chief complaint: Acute diarrhoea.
- Onset, duration, progression: Symptoms started about 3 days ago; currently 4–5 bowel movements per day; stool described as watery/loose with variable consistency; one episode of vomiting; mild fever possibly; appetite reduced but patient still able to drink fluids.
- Associated symptoms: Abdominal pain; no blood in stool; no mucus; able to maintain oral intake.
- Past medical history: Asthma.
- Medications: Lexapro (SSRI); asthma inhaler (name not clearly documented); allergies: none.
- Social history: Not explicitly detailed beyond family history.
- Family history: Father had hypertension; father died of bowel cancer at about 62.
- Allergies: None documented.

Objective:
- General: Patient appears well; not dehydrated at presentation; able to drink fluids.
- Vitals: Not documented in transcript.
- Physical exam: No detailed abdominal exam findings documented.
- Other: No laboratory tests or imaging results obtained or reported.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Issue: Acute gastroenteritis, likely viral
   - Assessment: Acute viral gastroenteritis is the most consistent diagnosis given abrupt onset (3 days), 4–5 loose stools/day, watery stool, one vomiting episode, mild fever possible, and preserved oral intake; patient appears well-hydrated.
   - Differentials (from DDx and consistent with transcript):
     - Acute bacterial gastroenteritis – Medium likelihood; plausible but less supported by history (no travel/exposure, no fever/toxicity).
     - SSRI-induced diarrhoea (Lexapro) – Medium likelihood; consider as contributing factor.
     - Inflammatory bowel disease flare – Low to medium likelihood; less likely given acute, short duration and absence of blood.
   - Investigations planned: Stool sample if diarrhoea persists ≥7 days or if blood/mucus appears; otherwise no immediate labs ordered.
   - Treatment planned: Oral rehydration (Dioralyte), maintain fluids; soft diet with gradual reintroduction of foods; avoid dairy, fish, meat, eggs during active diarrhoea; probiotic yogurt to support gut flora; monitor for dehydration or worsening symptoms; no antibiotics unless indicated by stool testing or clinical course.
   - Referrals: None at this time.

Quality checks (document quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements: Allergies documented as None; current medications include Lexapro and an asthma inhaler, but doses/routes/frequencies are not documented (recorded as “dose/route/frequency not documented” per policy). Vital signs and a physical exam were not documented beyond general appearance; no labs or imaging were performed.
- Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx: None detected; DDx items align with the presented history.
- Transcript quality: Clear overall; minor ambiguity around inhaler vs Lexapro naming noted in conversation.

Note: A COVID-19 vaccine suitability assessment was not mentioned in the transcript.

Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.
